title: Governor of Connecticut

context.text: Incumbent Democratic Gov. Ned Lamont is running for a third term. Connecticut governors have no term limit.

Lamont won the Democratic Party's convention endorsement over state Rep. Josh Elliott, 74.6% to 25.4%, then won the August 11 primary 67.9% to 32.1%; he was the first incumbent governor to face a primary since Ella Grasso in 1978.

State Sen. Ryan Fazio won the Republican convention endorsement on May 16 with about 92% of delegates after former New Britain Mayor Erin Stewart suspended her campaign; former New York Lt. Gov. Betsy McCaughey fell short of the 15% needed to force a primary.

Only Lamont and Fazio appear on the general-election ballot with party lines. Write-in campaigns by Christian Noe and Zenobia Adgers are listed for governor, and Politics1 also lists Lee Whitnum as a write-in.

candidates.name: Ned Lamont
candidates.ballotNote: Running with Lt. Gov. Susan Bysiewicz. Defeated state Rep. Josh Elliott in the August 11 Democratic primary, 67.9% to 32.1%.

summary.text: Ned Lamont is the incumbent Democratic Governor of Connecticut, seeking a third term with Lt. Gov. Susan Bysiewicz. A businessman who founded the cable-services company Campus Televideo, he won the governorship in 2018 and was re-elected in 2022. His campaign emphasizes lowering costs, universal pre-K and child care, housing supply and energy-cost oversight of utilities.

background.text: Born in Washington, D.C.; B.A. from Harvard College (1976) and M.B.A. from the Yale School of Management (1980).
Founded Campus Televideo, a cable and satellite services company for college campuses; served as a Greenwich selectman, 1987-1989.
Lost the 2006 U.S. Senate race to Joe Lieberman and the 2010 Democratic gubernatorial primary; won the governorship in 2018 and 2022.

priorities.text: Lowering costs for families through universal pre-K, expanded affordable child care, universal free school meals and more affordable health care.
Lowering electricity costs by making affordability a standard in utility regulation and strengthening oversight of utilities.
His 'Fair Share Healthcare Initiative,' requiring large employers with workers on HUSKY (Medicaid) to contribute up to $1,000 per employee.

positions.summary: Signed a 2022 law protecting patients who travel to Connecticut for abortion care and the providers who treat them, which his campaign calls the first such law after Roe v. Wade was overturned.
His campaign says he cracked down on ghost guns, banned open carry and expanded safe-storage requirements; he signed the 2023 Act Addressing Gun Violence (Public Act 23-53).
Signed the November 2025 housing growth act and lists reducing housing costs by increasing housing supply responsibly among his priorities.
His campaign cites raising the minimum wage to $15 per hour with automatic annual increases tied to inflation.
Campaign materials cite expanding the state's TRUST Act and barring federal immigration agents from wearing masks or making warrantless arrests inside Connecticut courthouses.

Priorities include universal pre-K and expanded affordable child care; his campaign describes moving toward free child care for families earning under $100,000 and capping costs for all families rather than child care free for all.

record.text: Signed Public Act 22-19, limiting the governor's discretion to extradite people over reproductive health care provided in Connecticut and creating protections for patients and providers.

Signed Public Act 23-53, An Act Addressing Gun Violence, which among other provisions prohibits carrying a firearm with intent to display it and adds provisions on firearms made from unfinished frames or lower receivers.

Signed Public Act 25-1 (HB 8002), An Act Concerning Housing Growth, enacted in a November 2025 special session; it creates a first-time homebuyer savings program and a new municipal housing growth planning framework.

candidates.name: Ryan Fazio
candidates.ballotNote: Running with Lt. Gov. candidate Matthew Corey, a bar owner. Won the Republican endorsement at the May 16 convention with about 92% of delegates; no primary was held.

summary.text: Ryan Fazio is a Republican state senator from Greenwich and the Republican and Independent Party nominee for governor, with running mate Matthew Corey. First elected in a 2021 special election, he is the ranking senator on the Energy and Technology Committee. His platform centers on cutting income taxes and electricity bills, capping property taxes and a 'Grand Bargain' on housing that protects local zoning control.

background.text: Grew up in Greenwich; B.A. in economics from Northwestern University (2012); worked mostly in the commodities industry and is now a financial advisor.
Won a 2021 special election for the 36th Senate district, ending the Democratic supermajority, and was re-elected in 2022 and 2024.

priorities.text: Cutting state income-tax rates, which his plan says would provide more than $2.5 billion in annual tax relief, and capping property taxes.
Cutting electricity bills by 20% by ending hidden taxes, expanding supply and removing mandates.
A 'Grand Bargain' on housing that lowers costs, grows supply and protects local control of zoning.

positions.summary: Proposes reducing state income-tax rates for every Connecticut family and capping property taxes.
positions.quote: Ryan's plan would lower income taxes for every Connecticut family by $1,500 and implement property tax caps.

positions.summary: Voted against the 2025 housing growth act (HB 8002), calling it flawed overall; his housing plan proposes streamlining permitting and incentivizing small-scale housing such as accessory dwelling units, but also rolling back HB 8002 and Section 8-30g to protect local zoning control.

record.text: Voted no on the final Senate passage of SB 1, the state budget adjustments for the biennium ending June 30, 2027, which passed 30-6.
Voted no on the final Senate passage of HB 5043, concerning convertible pistols and unfinished frames or lower receivers, which passed 22-11.
Voted no on the final Senate passage of HB 5468, concerning parent-managed learning, which passed 22-14.
Voted no on the final Senate passage of HB 8002, An Act Concerning Housing Growth, which passed 24-10 and which Gov. Lamont signed.

researchNotes: Running mates (Susan Bysiewicz, Matthew Corey) are elected jointly with the governor candidate and are noted in each candidate's ballotNote rather than listed separately. The slate was confirmed against official Connecticut Secretary of the State sample ballot (Westport): the governor race shows only two tickets, Lamont/Bysiewicz and Fazio/Corey, each on two party lines; the party-line names (Democratic, Working Families, Republican, Independent Party) come from Wikipedia's results table because the ballot text does not extract. Declared write-ins (Noe, Adgers, Whitnum) are not listed as candidates. Fazio's roll-call votes were read directly from the Connecticut General Assembly's Senate vote PDFs; bill titles and signing dates from the General Assembly's bill-status pages.
